hints.title: Name the repeated logarithm
hints.body: Put t=log2p and record the allowed domain of p. Substitute each point into the same straight-line equation.
hints.recap: Renaming a repeated expression can expose ordinary simultaneous equations.
hints.pitfall: Both points must lie on one line with the same gradient.
hints.pause: Write two equations in the line gradient and your new variable.

recall.reminder: Renaming a repeated expression can expose ordinary simultaneous equations.

hints.title: Keep both zero-product cases
hints.body: Use the point whose vertical coordinate equals the line intercept. Rearranging its equation produces a product equal to zero. Consider each factor separately.
hints.recap: A product is zero when at least one of its factors is zero.
hints.pitfall: Dividing by an unknown factor can discard a permitted solution.
hints.pause: Complete both cases using the other point, undo the logarithmic substitution and check both points.

recall.reminder: A product is zero when at least one of its factors is zero.

solution:
1. Substitute the two points. Let t=log2p, with p>0. The equations are t=3m+4 and 4=mt+4, so mt=0.

2. Examine both cases. If m=0, then t=4 and p=24=16. If t=0, then m=−4/3 and p=20=1.

3. Check. For p=16 both points lie on y=4. For p=1 the points are (3,0) and (0,4), lying on y=−43x+4. Both have positive logarithm arguments. Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Use a logarithmic coordinate substitution and preserve both zero-product line cases
